numericalRecipes.promptTemplate: Two deployments run p(x)=w*x+b. A uses w=2,b=-1. B uses w=2+{{dw}},b=-1+{{db}}. At x={{x}}, how much must you ADD to B's bias so both deployments agree on this input? Keep both slopes fixed. Enter one signed number.

A scalar state starts at w={{w}}. A completed backward pass stores g={{g}} but does not update w. The optimizer then executes w <- w-eta*g once, with eta=1. A second backward pass stores g=99, and execution stops before another optimizer call. What value of w belongs in a checkpoint at this boundary?

A split toy network has h=w*x, p=v*h and L=(p-y)^2/2. For x={{x}},w={{w}},v={{v}},y={{y}}, the second stage sends the correct scalar dL/dh. The first stage must still finish its chain rule. What dL/dw must it produce? No optimizer step occurs.

A dense tensor has shape ({{b}},{{t}},{{d}}), with 2 bytes per element. A transpose VIEW shares its allocation. Making one contiguous copy of that view allocates another equally sized payload. Ignoring metadata and allocator padding, how many payload bytes are live while the original and copy both remain reachable?

A rank-two view uses element offset = base+i*{{s0}}+j*{{s1}}, with 4 bytes per element. Both (i,j)=(1,2) and (2,0) are valid. What is address(2,0) MINUS address(1,2), in bytes? The shared base offset is unspecified because it cancels.
A=[[2,{{a}}],[0,3]] and B=[[1,4],[{{b}},-1]]. For C=A*B, enter C[0,0]+C[1,1], the trace of the product. Indices are zero based. Do not multiply corresponding entries elementwise.

Two scalar examples have residuals prediction-target equal to {{r}} and -{{r}}. The loss is their MEAN half-squared error. A debugging change doubles only the second residual. What is new loss minus old loss?
The parameter w is reused: u=w*w, p=u+{{c}}*w, L=(p-{{y}})^2/2. Evaluate dL/dw at w={{w}}. Count both operand paths through w*w.

A scalar optimizer starts at w={{w}} with recorded gradient g={{g}}. It applies ordinary descent with learning rate 1/{{d}}. A second optimizer call intentionally uses the SAME recorded gradient without a new backward pass. Return w after the second call.

A held-out report covers {{n}} examples with mean loss {{m}}. Its first example has loss {{a}} and is removed because it was duplicated. What is the mean over the remaining {{n}} minus one examples? Use the weighted loss total, not a mean of means.
Let u=x*x and z=u*u+{{c}}*u, with x={{x}}. In a reverse pass, what TOTAL adjoint must accumulate at the intermediate u before its multiplication is differentiated? Report dz/du, not dz/dx.

A logical batch has {{n}} examples with mean gradient {{g}}. One microbatch contains {{k}} of those examples and has mean gradient {{a}}. What SUM of per-example gradients must the remaining examples contribute? No update occurs between microbatches.
At x={{x}}, u=x*x and z=u+x. backward(root,seed) clears ALL adjoints before propagation. Call backward(z,3), then backward(u,2), without changing x. Return x.grad after the second call only.
A scalar two-unit MLP at x={{x}} has h0=ReLU(2*x-1), h1=ReLU(-x-1), p=3*h0+2*h1, L=(p-{{y}})^2/2. What is dL/dx? All approved inputs keep both preactivations away from zero.
A scalar stack applies x1=x0+F1(x0), x2=x1+F2(x1), where F1(x)=x/{{a}} and F2(x)=-x/{{b}}. At x0=1, enter dx2/dx0. The skip paths remain present in BOTH blocks.
Momentum uses m_new=(1/2)*m_old+g and w_new=w_old-(1/4)*m_new. Start w=3,m={{m}}. Use gradient {{g}} on step one and gradient zero on step two. Return w after BOTH updates; momentum is retained.

A bias-only regressor predicts w, with loss (w-y)^2/2 and learning rate 1/2. Start w={{w}}. Recompute and clear gradients each step. First train on y={{a}}, then on a DIFFERENT example y={{b}}. Return w after step two.

A packed loss report has three valid token losses 1,2,{{x}} and two padded entries with loss 100 each. The desired mean is over valid tokens. A bug divides the valid loss sum by all five positions. Enter correct mean minus buggy mean.

An append-only KV cache has {{l}} layers, batch {{b}}, {{h}} KV heads, head width {{d}}, and 2 bytes per cached scalar. Both keys and values are cached. Its length grows from 5 to 8 tokens. How many ADDITIONAL payload bytes are needed, excluding allocation slack?

A bias-free attention module has D={{d}}, Q width {{q}}, K width {{q}}, and V width {{v}}. Its output projection maps width {{v}} back to D. If you omit ONLY the K projection from a parameter ledger, how many parameters are missing? Count scalar weights, not activations.

Hold model width D={{d}}, query heads Hq=4 and head width 2 fixed. Change KV heads from 4 to 1, retaining Q and output projections unchanged. There are no biases. How many projection parameters are SAVED by this grouped-query change?

A decoder ties its token embedding and output vocabulary matrix: one V by D parameter allocation serves both roles. V={{v}},D={{d}},T={{t}}. Learned position embeddings have T by D entries. Other weights are unaffected. A ledger mistakenly counts a separate vocabulary output matrix. How many parameters does it overcount?

For p=w*x and half-squared loss, w={{w}}. Backward on (x=2,y=1) runs first. Then the gradient is explicitly cleared. Backward on (x=3,y=2) runs TWICE with fresh forward graphs but no intervening clear or optimizer call. Return the final w.grad.

A synthetic asynchronous trace is: previous work completes at t=11ms; measured launch starts t=14ms; CPU submission ends t=16ms; measured device work completes t={{end}}ms. Synchronization before t=14 has already finished. How many milliseconds does submission-only timing UNDERREPORT the measured interval?

A lazy scalar training graph represents L=(w*x-y)^2/2 at w={{w}},x=2,y=1. The planned descent step has eta=1/4. Before materialization, host code changes an unrelated scalar variable named w to 99; the graph captured the ORIGINAL numeric value. Once evaluated, what updated parameter value does this graph produce?

A frozen bias-free matrix has shape ({{o}},{{i}}). An adapter uses B of shape (out,r) and A of shape (r,in). Compare rank 2 with rank 3, both with no other trainable weights. How many ADDITIONAL trainable scalars does rank 3 introduce?

Two unfused stages materialize an intermediate with shape ({{r}},{{c}}), 4 bytes per element. A fused path removes the intermediate write and later read, but additionally reads a separate r-element bias vector once. Count that entire new bias read. What is NET payload bytes saved under this explicit traffic model?

A hypothetical memory budget is {{p}} GiB physical with {{o}} GiB reserved for the OS/other processes. Parameters, gradients and optimizer state together occupy {{s}} GiB. Activations need 7 GiB but checkpointing reduces them to 3 GiB. After that change, how much usable headroom remains? Use GiB consistently and ignore allocator overhead.

Two replicas each report a mean gradient: replica A has {{a}} examples with mean 2; replica B has {{b}} examples with mean -1. The correct logical-batch gradient is their sample-weighted mean. What TOTAL gradient sum, before division by the total example count, should the merge use?

A forward-only pipeline has {{s}} equal stages, each taking {{t}} ms per microbatch, no communication overhead and no overlap inside one stage. Sending {{m}} microbatches together takes fill plus drain time. How many milliseconds are SAVED compared with sending those microbatches strictly one at a time through all stages?

Synthetic outer update: old weight w={{w}}, two local weights w-1 and w-3. Form g as the mean of old-minus-local pseudo-gradients. Start momentum m=2, update m_new=(1/2)*m+g, then use Nesterov direction g+(1/2)*m_new with learning rate 1/4. Return new weight. No local dataset weighting is implied.

A synthetic supervisor deadline is t={{deadline}}s after spawn. The executable starts at t=2, readiness succeeds at t={{ready}}, and admission succeeds at t={{admit}}. How many seconds of deadline margin exist at ADMISSION? Neither process creation nor readiness is admission.

A synthetic 20-block model is split at half-open boundaries [0,{{h}}), [{{h}},{{t}}), [{{t}},20). Blocks execute once in increasing order. If the middle process and tail process are combined, how many block invocations does their combined forward perform? Embeddings and output heads are not counted as blocks.

Synthetic monotonic timestamps in seconds: spawn=2, registration=7, forward completed=13, backward completed={{b}}, upload acknowledged={{u}}. What is upload-acknowledgment time minus backward-completion time? Treat this as an event interval; it does not measure GPU execution or credit.
Reference tensor is [10,-10,2,-2]; candidate is [{{a}},-{{a}},2,-2]. Signed sums agree. What is their maximum coordinatewise absolute error?

One microbatch contains {{n}} examples, each with gradient 2. Another contains ONE example with gradient 8. A candidate averages the two microbatch means equally. Enter candidate gradient minus the correct example-weighted mean.

A serial reference run spends {{c}} seconds in the optimized computation and {{o}} seconds elsewhere. The new computation is twice as fast BUT adds {{h}} seconds of setup on the measured path. Return full-run speedup old_time/new_time.

A strictly serial toy job computes for {{c}} seconds, sends 150 decimal MB over a sustained 100 Mbit/s link, and performs {{o}} seconds of other work. A compression pass costs 1 second and halves ONLY the payload size. What is the net reduction in total wall time, in seconds? No overlap or protocol overhead is assumed.
For F(a,b)=a*a*b+sin(b), evaluate the directional derivative at (a,b)=(1,0) along direction (da,db)=({{da}},{{db}}). The direction is NOT normalized. Return grad(F) dot direction.
